passage: At the small cooperative bank branch in Nabha, Amandeep watched how Nilesh worked. When the regional manager visited, Nilesh was all smiles and stories, presenting the new farmer-loan filing system as his own. Amandeep and the two clerks had built it over the monsoon, while Nilesh called their work "just typing". The clerks grumbled in the back room, and one stopped staying late. Amandeep didn't rant or try to out-charm him. That evening she took out the register where she had logged every change with dates and names, and wrote a short, plain note to the manager listing who had done which part. At the next meeting she asked that each clerk present their own section.

qa.q: When did Amandeep and the clerks build the filing system?
qa.a: They built it over the monsoon.

qa.q: What might the clerk who stopped staying late be feeling?
qa.a: The clerk probably feels unappreciated and discouraged after Nilesh called their work "just typing".

qa.q: What choice did Amandeep make instead of ranting, and why was it wise?
qa.a: She used her dated register to write a plain note on who did what and asked each clerk to present, keeping to facts and protecting morale.

qa.q: How might the regional manager see things after reading Amandeep's note?
qa.a: The manager would likely get a clearer, fairer picture of the work than Nilesh's charm gave.

grounding: A bank officer sees a colleague take credit and belittle others while charming seniors, and answers with records and facts rather than competition.
